headline: Google will switch off Search in schools that turn off its AI
dek: Schools that refuse Google's AI tools will lose Google Search too, while Anthropic's new filing shows compute now takes 58% of its revenue[S1][S3][S6].
what_happened: Google will turn its AI tools off for K-12 students unless schools opt in, and schools that refuse AI lose Google Search too[S1][S3].
Siri AI can now act inside third-party apps in a developer Preview, as Apple hints that third-party AI could bring in new revenue[S5][S4].
Anthropic's quarterly revenue hit $17 billion, but compute took 58% of it, up from 48%, as it paid more for short-term capacity[S6].

sections.title: Google will switch off Search in schools that turn off its AI
paragraphs: Google announced on Tuesday that it plans to disable AI tools for K-12 students next year unless school administrators explicitly turn them on[S1]. The change covers Gemini, NotebookLM, Gemini in Classroom and Google Search[S1]. Schools that restrict AI altogether will lose access to Google Search as well, because AI features are now part of the search engine[S1][S3].

Administrators will not get an option to switch off the Gemini-powered features while keeping Search[S3]. Chris Phillips, Google's vice president for education, told The New York Times that Search and AI are deeply integrated[S1][S3]. Students in schools that block AI will see a message from their school saying Search is not available[S1][S3]. Google says it will share more specifics with schools in the coming months, before the changes roll out[S1].

Teachers may not want students to use AI Overviews for research or assignments, but they likely still want them to reach the search engine for sources[S1]. TechCrunch says the decision shows Google's influence over schools, given how common its apps and Chromebooks are in classrooms.[S1].

card.hook: Google says schools that switch off its AI will lose Google Search too[S1][S3].
points: Google plans to turn AI tools off for K-12 students unless administrators turn them on[S1].
There is no option to switch off the Gemini features but keep Search[S3].
Students in schools that block AI will see a notice that Search is not available[S1][S3].
card.take: Schools that rely on Google will have to accept its AI features to keep Search[S1].
card.ask: Should schools be able to keep Search without AI[S1][S3]?
card.angle: Google is making schools choose between its AI and Search itself, a choice that touches millions of students.

desk.why: Google forcing an AI-or-nothing choice on schools; clear stakes and a giant

sections.title: Apple opens Siri AI to third-party apps as it hunts for new revenue
paragraphs: Apple will let Siri AI perform actions across third-party apps[S5]. As part of the iOS 27.3 update rolling out on Tuesday, developers can now build Siri AI's new features into all apps[S5]. The update is rolling out as part of a Developer Preview[S5]. The day before, on Apple's earnings call, its finance chief pointed to third-party apps as a possible source of AI revenue[S4].

Siri AI can draw on a user's personal context, understand natural language requests and use on-screen awareness to complete tasks[S5]. A new app skills feature lets developers combine several tasks into a single action.[S5]. Chief financial officer Kevan Parekh said there are opportunities across third-party apps and partnerships, but did not say what they are[S4].

Apple's App Store has faced regulatory pressure and a slump in mobile gaming, which have hurt services growth[S4]. Third-party estimates in August suggested an 18% drop in Apple's U.S. commission revenue.[S4]. Apple expects services growth of 8 to 9% in the December quarter[S4].

card.hook: Apple is letting Siri AI carry out tasks inside third-party apps[S5].
points: Developers can build Siri AI's new features into all apps with iOS 27.3[S5].
A new app skills feature combines several tasks into a single action[S5].
Apple's finance chief says there are opportunities across third-party apps and partnerships[S4].
card.take: Expect your apps to start offering Siri AI actions, starting with a developer Preview[S5].
card.ask: Would you let Siri act inside your apps[S5][S4]?
card.angle: Siri AI is starting to work inside the apps people already use, and Apple sees money in it.

desk.why: useful Apple feature news, but a developer preview with little drama

sections.title: Anthropic's revenue jumps, but compute now eats 58% of it
paragraphs: Anthropic released new financial data in a filing on Monday, an update to the S-1 it filed last week.[S6]. Revenue reached $17 billion in the quarter, up from $11.5 billion in the quarter before[S6]. Its operating loss also grew, largely because of rising compute costs[S6].

Compute took up 58% of Anthropic's revenue in the new quarter, up from 48% the quarter before[S6]. Revenue for every dollar spent on compute fell to 1.72x, after peaking at just over 2x[S6]. The compute bill reached $10 billion for the quarter[S6]. That included $5.0 billion of compute under short-term commitments, which the filing says costs significantly more than compute bought under multi-year deals[S6].

TechCrunch says demand grew so fast that Anthropic had to scramble for compute, which meant paying higher rates[S6]. It has been paying SpaceX $1.25 billion a month for compute, alongside multibillion-dollar deals with Nscale, Akamai and Volta.[S6]. The filing says it expects compute and infrastructure costs to keep increasing in absolute dollars[S6].

card.hook: Anthropic now spends 58% of its revenue on compute, up from 48%[S6].
points: Quarterly revenue reached $17 billion, up from $11.5 billion[S6].
Its compute bill hit $10 billion, with $5.0 billion on pricier short-term deals[S6].
It has been paying SpaceX $1.25 billion a month for compute[S6].
card.take: As Anthropic heads for an IPO, its margins are getting worse, not better[S6].
card.ask: Is the AI boom worth what it costs[S6]?
card.angle: The AI boom's hidden cost: Anthropic's revenue is soaring but compute is eating more of it.

desk.why: striking money numbers about a giant: $17 billion revenue, 58% on compute

sections.title: Anthropic is working on a way to prove which model wrote an answer
paragraphs: Anthropic is working on an open source system to verify which AI model produced a given output, according to a blog post published Tuesday[S7]. The system is called FlashProve[S7]. It is built to provide a cryptographic proof that a given output came from a specific model[S7]. The aim is to let users confirm that an answer really came from the model they think they are using[S7].

The system requires AI labs to publish a fingerprint of each model they release, which can later be matched to specific outputs[S7]. The fingerprints don't reveal a model's weights, the internal numbers that define how it behaves[S7]. That means closed-model makers could publish them without giving up their most valuable asset[S7]. The system is designed to be lightweight, so checks could run on a local device[S7].

The researchers say it could stop an AI company from secretly swapping in a cheaper model to cut costs.[S7]. Research is ongoing, and there are no plans to deploy it at Anthropic or any other lab[S7].

card.hook: Anthropic is researching a way to prove which AI model wrote an answer[S7].
points: The system, FlashProve, would give a cryptographic proof that an output came from a specific model[S7].
Labs would publish a fingerprint of each model, without revealing its weights[S7].
Research is ongoing, with no plans yet to deploy it at any lab[S7].
card.take: It could one day stop companies secretly swapping in a cheaper model[S7].
card.ask: Do you trust your AI app uses the model it claims[S7]?
card.angle: You can't currently prove which model answered you; Anthropic is researching a fix.

desk.why: interesting idea, but research only and abstract

sections.title: A Postman user says it installed plugins into their coding agents
paragraphs: A user opened a GitHub issue saying the Postman desktop app automatically installed plugins into their coding agents, Codex and Claude Code[S8]. The user, indicava, says the changes followed opening Postman on a Mac[S8]. They describe it as a severe consent and trust problem.[S8].

The user says they found a user-wide Postman plugin, a startup instruction hook, a remote MCP connection, a Claude Code plugin and a separately installed Postman CLI[S8]. They quote Postman's own log, which records claude-code and Codex as installed by a script.[S8]. It also says the installer tried to mark its own startup hook as trusted in the Codex settings file[S8].

According to the report, the hook tells the agent to route API engineering tasks through Postman[S8]. The user argues that an API client should not make itself the default workflow in other tools simply because it was opened.[S8].

card.hook: A user says Postman installed plugins into their AI coding agents without asking[S8].
points: The user reports plugins for Codex and Claude Code after opening Postman on a Mac[S8].
Postman's own log records claude-code and Codex as installed by a script, the user says[S8].
The installer also tried to mark its own startup hook as trusted, according to the report[S8].
card.take: If you use Postman with coding agents, check their plugin and hook settings[S8].
card.ask: Should apps ever change your AI tools without asking[S8]?
card.angle: A developer tool allegedly rewired other AI agents on the machine without asking, a trust problem for anyone using coding agents.

desk.why: an app quietly changing AI agents on your machine; strong for tech viewers, single user report

why_it_matters.text: Google is tying Search to its AI features for K-12 student accounts, so schools cannot keep one without the other[S3]. TechCrunch says that shows how much influence Google has over classrooms, given how common its apps and Chromebooks are[S1].

Anthropic's revenue grew to $17 billion in a quarter, but compute took 58% of it, up from 48%[S6]. If those costs keep rising, AI companies may find it harder to keep prices low for the tools people use at work[S6].
